arxiv-2508-16672.title: The AI Model Risk Catalog: What Developers and Researchers Miss About Real-World AI Harms
arxiv-2508-16672.creator: Pooja S. B. Rao, Sanja Šćepanović, Dinesh Babu Jayagopi, Mauro Cherubini, Daniele Quercia
arxiv-2508-16672.description: Abstract We analyzed nearly 460,000 AI model cards from Hugging Face to examine how developers report risks. From these, we extracted around 3,000 unique risk mentions and built the AI Model Risk Catalog . We compared these with risks identified by researchers in the MIT Risk Repository and with real-world incidents from the AI Incident Database.

arxiv-2510-10343.title: Learning the Exact SABR Model
arxiv-2510-10343.creator: Giorgia Rensi, Pietro Rossi, Marco Bianchetti
arxiv-2510-10343.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Giorgia Rensi, Pietro Rossi, Marco Bianchetti. The SABR model is a cornerstone of interest rate volatility modeling, but its practical application relies heavily on the analytical approximation by Hagan et al., whose accuracy deteriorates for high volatility, long maturities, and out-of-the-money options, admitting arbitrage. While machine learning approaches have been proposed to overcome these limitations, they have often been limited by simplified SABR dynamics or a lack of systematic validation against the full spectrum of market conditions.

pmc-12849248.creator: Emma Stirling-Cameron, Esteban Valencia, Kate Shannon, Haoxuan Zhou, Ran Hu, Grace Chong, Kaylee Ramage, Jennie Pearson, Shira Miriam Goldenberg

pmc-13216764.title: Pink–White Esthetic Optimization in Excessive Gingival Display Using Crown Lengthening and Direct Composite Veneering
pmc-13216764.creator: Nihangma Patangwa, Sanjay Kumar Sah, Hamoun Sabri
pmc-13216764.description: An esthetic smile plays a pivotal role in enhancing patient confidence and social well‐being. Smile esthetics are influenced by multiple factors, including maxillary anterior tooth morphology, lip length and mobility, periodontal health, and the degree of gingival display. Short clinical crowns associated with excessive gingival display are generally perceived as unesthetic and frequently require esthetic crown lengthening.

pmc-13249773.title: Impaired Iron-Copper Metabolic Axis in Human Intestinal Mucosa After Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass: A Prospective Transcriptomic Study Using Double-Balloon Enteroscopy
pmc-13249773.creator: Camila Shimizu, Dan Linetzky Waitzberg, Raquel Susana Torrinhas, Steven B. Heymsfield, Mariana Doce Passadore, Priscila Sala
pmc-13249773.description: BackgroundRoux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) effectively leads to weight loss in patients with severe obesity but is often accompanied by refractory iron deficiency. The molecular mechanisms governing the human intestinal copper-iron metabolic axis post-surgery remain poorly defined. This study evaluated the longitudinal impact of RYGB on intestinal gene expression related to micronutrient homeostasis.
